data.content_ref: inline:The mechanism field concludes with the sentence 'Unlike every previously studied system of this kind, which faced identical structural constraints yet exhibited none of this behaviour.' This is an unsupported universal negative comparative claim that is contextually incoherent with the rest of the mechanism. The mechanism describes a philosophical decision-procedure (Popperian critical rational choice via severe testing), not an empirical phenomenon observed across multiple systems. No 'previously studied systems' are identified, no evidence supports the claim that all of them faced 'identical structural constraints' yet 'exhibited none of this behaviour,' and the sentence does not contribute to explaining how the preference for corroborated theories operates. The claim is a sweeping universal quantification over an undefined class, presented without any derivation, premise, or reference. This spurious assertion undermines the internal coherence of the mechanism: a Popperian defense that prides itself on rejecting unjustified universal claims should not itself rest on one.
